One day, Mark was on his way home from school after class. Along the way, he saw a boy about the same age as him walking in front, dropping the bag he was carrying on his shoulder, which contained many books, two sweaters, a pair of gloves, and a playing stick. baseball and a tape recorder. Mark helped him pick up things scattered on the street. And because they were both going in the same direction, Mark helped him carry some things. While walking and talking, Mark learned that his name was Bill, he loved video games, was having a lot of trouble (bad grades) with his school subjects, and had just broken up with his girlfriend. Following the path they took to Bill's house first, Mark was invited by him to come in for a drink and watch some TV movies. That afternoon passed relatively comfortably with small laughs and heart-to-heart talks. Then Mark returned home. From then on, the two continued to meet each other, sometimes at school or out to lunch together… Then they both graduated from middle school, entered the same high school and remained friends for many years. Later. When the long years of high school ended, three weeks before graduation, Bill said he had something to tell Mark. Bill recalled the day many years ago when they first met on the way home from school. "Have you ever wondered why I carried so many things home that day?", Bill asked and then answered himself: "That day I cleaned out my locker at school because I didn't I wanted to leave a mess for the users after me. I stole some sleeping pills from my mother and that day I was on my way home to commit suicide. But after meeting you, talking and laughing with you, I realized that if I killed myself, I would lose the opportunity to have fun like I had with you and probably lose many more opportunities after that. . You see, Mark, when you helped me pick up the scattered objects on the road that day, you actually helped me much more than that. You saved my life".
A good deed, no matter how small, has a great meaning

In a certain garden, there are two grapefruit trees, one is Ta grapefruit, the other is Dien grapefruit. Dien grapefruit has a lot of fruit, while Ta grapefruit has very little fruit and is less sweet. However, the boss loves these two grapefruit trees very much. One day the boss had to go away for a long time, and a storm came to the garden. The wind was very strong, the rain was very heavy, the Dien grapefruit tree was not strong enough to withstand the storm, so the Ta grapefruit tree used its body to protect the Dien grapefruit tree from being broken by the storm, it shouted in the storm: 
	 - Just broke a few branches, I don't want to see you give up. Thus, both grapefruit trees relied on each other to overcome the storm. After the storm, both survived but both had broken branches, especially the Ta grapefruit tree. Seeing this, the boss's nephew immediately decided to bring an ax to cut down the Ta grapefruit tree to clear land for the Dien grapefruit tree to grow. The grapefruit tree saw this and was extremely worried about his friend. He immediately thought of a plan. He invited the worms in the garden to crawl on the two grapefruit trees so that the owner would be afraid to cut down the trees. Indeed, after seeing worms covering two grapefruit trees, the young master threw away the ax and ran away, waiting for his grandfather to return. When the boss returned, the boy curiously asked: 
	 - Ta grapefruit tree bears little fruit and is not delicious, so why don't you cut it down? His grandfather replied: 
	 - Because it was a grapefruit tree that one of his teammates brought from the south to give to him, it was proof of his friendship, after many years of separation, he still always remembers each other and remembers his friend. shared the sweetness together, fought together. Although our grapefruit is not delicious, to him it is always as sweet as his eternal friendship.
Friendship

In a small house, there lived a boy and a dog named Lizzi. The boy loved his dog very much. Suddenly one day he discovered that his dog had a problem so he decided to take him to the doctor. The dog suffered from retinal degeneration and was permanently blind. From then on, Lizzi became bored, had low self-esteem, and was not interested in eating or going for walks with her master. One day the owner brought another dog home, named Mart. When Mart arrived home, he asked about getting to know Lizzi. But the blind dog ignored all the new dog's efforts, he shouted: 
	 - I'm just a useless blind dog, I can't walk, I can't have fun. Even the master hates me, so he brought you back to replace me. You don't have to act like you care about me! Mart heard that and was extremely sad: 
	 - I'm really sorry, I didn't know you were blind. But that doesn't affect us being friends. I will be your friend, I will have fun with you, I will be your eyes. From then on, the two dogs became close and lived beautiful years together in their house. One day, the master brought Lizzi to his friend. Hearing the news, Mart was sad, stopped eating and drinking, and finally snuck out to look for his friend. After a lot of effort, Mart found Lizzi, The dog also refused to eat or drink because he missed his friend. Touched by the friendship of the two dogs, their owner decided not to separate the two. And so the blind dog followed Mart's instructions and returned to his house.
Light of friendship

The shop owner hung a "Puppies for sale" sign on the door. Such signs are always attractive to younger customers. Just then, a boy appeared. 
	 – How much do you sell these dogs for? – asked the boy. The owner replied: 
	 – Between $30 and $50. The boy took out some change from his pocket. “I have $2.37,” he said, “can I look at them?” The shopkeeper smiled and whistled. From the kennel ran out the mother dog Lady, with five pretty little furry clutches following. A puppy hobbled to the last run. Immediately, the boy pointed to the little dog with a paralyzed leg: "What's wrong with this puppy?" The owner explained that the vet looked at it and said the puppy had a hip defect. It will be limping forever. It will always be lame. The child was very emotional: “I want to buy that puppy.” The owner said: 
	 – You probably don't want to buy that dog, but if you want it, I'll give it to you. The boy was angry. He looked his master straight in the eye, and said: 
	 – I don't want you to give me that puppy. It deserves it like any other and I'll pay you full price for it. Actually, I'll give you $2.37 now and 50 cents a month until I pay the full amount. Owner objected: 
	 – I don't want to buy that dog. It will never be able to run and play with you like other puppies. Hearing that, the boy crouched down and pulled up the leg of his pants to reveal a shriveled leg that had to be supported by a brace system. He looked up at his master and said very quietly: 
	 – Yeah, I can't run either, and that little dog needs a friend who can understand him!
Friend

A boy invited his mother to attend his first parent-teacher conference in elementary school. What the boy feared came true, his mother accepted. This was the first time his friends and homeroom teacher met the boy's mother and he was very embarrassed about his mother's appearance. Although she was also a beautiful woman, she had a large scar that covered nearly the entire right side of her face. The boy never wanted to ask his mother why he had such a big scar. At the meeting, everyone had a very nice impression of the mother's gentleness and natural beauty despite the scar, but the boy was still shy and hid himself in a corner to avoid everyone. There, the boy heard his mother talking to the teacher. "How did you get such a scar on your face?" His teacher asked. The mother replied, "When my child was a baby, he was in his room when a fire broke out." Everyone was afraid to go in because the fire was so high, so I ran in. When I ran to it, I saw a beam falling on it and I quickly covered it with myself. I was beaten until I fainted, but luckily a firefighter came in and saved both me and my child." The Mother touched the wrinkled scar on her face. "This scar can no longer be cured, but Until this day, I have never regretted what I did." At this point, the boy ran out of his hiding place towards his mother, tears in his eyes. The boy hugged his mother and felt her presence. Mother's sacrifice for him. The boy held his mother's hand tightly all day as if he did not want to let go.
Mother\'s love

Where is my child? The young mother asked in joy after a tiring labor. With a radiant face, she took the child from the doctor's hands. However, the smile suddenly faded from her lips when she saw that the baby's external ear structure was different from other children. However, the child was still lucky to hear and understand normally. This means the child's inner ear structure is still well developed. However, the mother still couldn't help but worry about her child's disability. That makes the mother feel even more sorry and feel sorry for her child. On the contrary, the child is still carefree and happy, unaware of his disability. Until one day, the boy came home from school and hugged his mother, then burst into tears: "Mom! My friends tease me, they say I'm a child with an 'earless' ear!" A child's words are like a knife cutting into a mother's heart. Holding her child tightly in her arms, the mother seemed to embrace all her pain. Then in that moment, the boy suddenly stopped crying. Turning to look at his mother, the boy firmly said: "I will prove to everyone that although I am physically disabled, I will not be mentally disabled. Don't cry anymore, Mom!" As the days pass, the child grows up with physical disabilities. As if to prove his promise, the boy is always dedicated to studying and constantly strives to explore and learn things beyond books. The boy also showed outstanding talent in literature and vocal music. The boy's academic achievements were so excellent that the teachers always assured the boy's parents that, if he continued to cultivate and practice, he would be a talent of the country. How can I express the joy a mother feels when she sees her child's achievements? Now, the mother has begun to feel more at ease about her child's flaws, although deep down in her heart, she still wishes for her child to be physically healthy. One day, the boy's life seemed to open up with a new ray of hope. Specialists confirmed that he could receive an ear transplant, as long as someone agreed to donate his ear. So the mother and father embarked on a search for someone who could donate their child's ear. One day, the father returned home with an excited face and announced: "I have found someone willing to donate my ear to you." The surgery was successful, the boy received a pair of soft, perfect ears. However, the boy could not find the person who donated his ear. It was said that that person wanted to be sacrificed silently and decided not to reveal his identity. Then the boy grew up and became a famous musician. His fame goes beyond the ocean and reaches neighboring countries. At this time, that boy became a successful and rich person. However, he is always worried about not being able to repay the person who donated his ears. Occasionally, during the rare times he visited his parents, the young man asked his father for information about his benefactor, but his father only shook his head in despair. And the mother, as always, quietly let down her hair and sat quietly in a warm corner of the room looking at him. It seems that old age soon caught up with her and that caused her personality to change. Since the day the son received an ear transplant and began to live an independent life, the mother gradually became distant. She no longer talked to her son, and sometimes the boy even felt like his mother was trying to avoid him. "Maybe my mother is angry because I'm not with her often anymore," the boy still feels guilty about that. However, caught up in the whirlwind of work, he continued to leave his family for his long tours. One day, the boy learned that his mother was seriously ill. Taking the earliest flight home, he rushed to the hospital with his mother. Watching his mother take her last breaths on the hospital bed, the young man bent down to hug his mother and sobbed. The young man kissed the thin hands that had spent years raising him. He kissed his mother's forehead marked with time-worn wrinkles, then, trembling, he gently stroked his mother's white hair. Suddenly he realized in shock: his mother no longer had ears. Now I understand why for so many years, my mother has always tried to stay away from me… I also realized the truth that for many years, my mother has never cut her hair, rarely leaves the house and rarely socializes. Communicate with people around you. Weeping, the young man knelt down next to his mother, hugging her small body. He kissed her cheeks and forehead with loving kisses and whispered: "Mom!" Mom gave me life and gave me my whole life!”.
Please don\'t make mom cry

Roses for mom

There was a poor mother, she had a son. She loves this son very much. Even though the family is very poor, she always tries to find ways for her son to go to school and study. Her daily job is to carry bags and go from house to house to ask for handfuls of rice so that her children can be full and have money to go to school. Every day, she left very early and went very far from home. Because she knew that if she let her son and the neighbors know, her son would be embarrassed and refuse to go to school anymore, so she went to places far away from where she lived to ask for handfuls of rice. Every day like that and then many years passed, her son was able to enter college with handfuls of rice that his mother begged for without even knowing that she did the job of begging for rice every day. The day he entered school was also the day his mother became old and the cost of admission weighed heavily on her old mother's shoulders. In those days, at school, students would stay in boarding schools, so each family would have to send rice to the kitchen to cook for the students to eat that month. At the beginning of every month, the mother brings a few hundred thousand for her son and a bag of rice for the kitchen. She did not let her son know, she quietly walked from the back gate of the school to bring rice to the kitchen. When he arrived at the kitchen, the chef saw an old woman with a wrinkled face, a hunched back, deep eyes and tanned skin. The chef asked her where she was going, and she said, "I brought rice to give to my son." The chef opened the bag of rice to check. When the bag of rice was opened, the chef felt surprised and annoyed and said, "Bring the rice back." We don't accept that many types of rice in the same bag. The old woman lowered her head and said with a pleading look, "My family is very poor. I really only have rice like this. Please accept it for me, thank you." Seeing the poor old woman's face, the chef accepted it and said: "Next time I won't accept rice like this again!". After speaking, the old woman bowed her head in thanks and quietly walked away. Then another month passed and she did the same job as last month, she brought a bag of rice with many types of rice like last month, one for each type and she also tried to beg the chef to accept it, this time he was very happy. Reported harshly to her but still accepted. In his heart, he told himself that next month I will no longer accept this rice from her, cooking rice is very difficult. Then another month passed, the old woman still brought the same rice as before, this time the chef scolded her: "I told you, I won't accept this rice anymore. Please bring it home!”. I will report this to the principal. This time, she sat down on the ground, her back was bent because she had to carry bags everywhere to ask for rice every day." Tears began to roll down her thin face. Then she said: “I'm sorry, but there's really no other way. I beg you not to tell the principal, I beg you not to let my son know, if he knew he wouldn't want to go to school anymore, because this is the rice I beg for every day to get, that's why he's like that." The cook was silent, then sat down, helped the old woman sit and said: "I'm sorry, I don't know about this. I will report this to the Principal but I won't let your child know, you can rest assured."
The beggar mother

A man has two large pots to carry water. One of the pots had a crack, so when I brought the water from the well, the water in the pot was only half. The intact pot is proud of its perfection, and the cracked pot is always tormented by not being able to complete the task. One of the pots has a crack One day the cracked pot said to its owner, “I am ashamed of myself. I want to apologize to you!”. 
	 – “What are you ashamed of?” 
	 – “It is only because of my fault that you do not get what you deserve!” 
	 – “No, when you go back, pay attention to the flower beds by the roadside”. 
	 Indeed, along the roadside are brilliant flower beds. The cracked pot felt happy for a while, but when it got home it was still half full of water. 
	 – “I’m sorry sir!” Flowers only grow on this side of the road 
	 – “Didn't you notice that flowers only grow on this side of the road, on your side? I knew your flaw and took advantage of it. I planted flower seeds on your side of the road, and over the years you have happily watered them. I pick those petals to decorate the house. Without you, my house would not be as cozy and charming as this." Each of us is like a cracked pot – make use of our cracks.
Cracked pot

In a certain forest, there were three ancient trees discussing the future. The first tree said: "One day, I want to become a treasure box with a splendid shape." The second tree said: “I want to become a big boat. I will carry the queen and the king around the world." And the third tree: "I want to grow to become the biggest tree in this forest. Everyone who looks up the hill will see me reaching far, touching the sky."

	 A year later, a group of people went to the forest and sawed the tree trunks. All three smiled happily because they believed their wishes would come true. When the first tree was sold to a carpenter, it was made into a cattle trough and placed in a barn covered with a layer of grass. The second tree was sold to a boat builder who made a small boat for fishing. The third tree was cut into pieces and thrown back into the darkness. This is not what they expected. One day, a couple came to the barn. The wife had given birth, the husband hoped to find a cradle for the baby and the patch of grass became a warm place for the baby. The first tree feels its importance and understands that it is protecting a small life. A few years later, some people going fishing on a boat from the second tree encountered a big storm. The people on the boat were very tired, but the second tree knew that it had enough stability to keep its owner safe and peaceful. With the third tree, one day, someone came and picked up the logs. At the top of the hill, it is built into a fence to prevent wild animals. When the sun just came out, the third tree realized that it had enough strength to stand on top of this hill. When things don't happen as you want, don't despair because everything happens on purpose. All three ancient trees fulfilled their dreams, even though the way to reach the final destination was not as expected. Life will not fail those who have heart.
Three ancient trees

A boy saw a cocoon of a butterfly. One day the cocoon opened a small slit, and the boy sat quietly and watched the butterfly for several hours as it struggled to get through the small crevice. But it seems it achieves nothing. It seemed that it had tried its best and couldn't go any further, so it stopped. The boy decided to help the butterfly Therefore, the boy decided to help the butterfly. He took the cocoon and cut the slit of the cocoon to make it bigger. The butterfly came out right away. But its body is swollen and tiny, its wings shrink. The boy continued to watch the butterfly, hoping that the wings would be big enough to support its body. But nothing happened. That butterfly will have to spend a lifetime In fact, that butterfly would have to spend its entire life crawling with its swollen body and contracted wings. It never flies. The boy, though kind but hasty, did not understand that it was the tight cocoon that caused the butterfly to struggle to get out that was the natural condition for the fluid in its body to move into the wing, to it can fly when it comes out of the cocoon.

	 A student who had just graduated from university and was looking for a job participated in a specialized innovation contest organized by a federation of universities throughout the country. After many month-long preliminary rounds, he was included in the group of best people to participate in the final round. Then he struggled to overcome his opponents in the final battle of wits, which lasted three tense days and won the first prize. His reward was a large amount of money that he had never dreamed of in his student life. After leaving the hall and quickly hiding from the camera lights of the press, he went into the parking lot to get his car and left. Suddenly a woman approached him. She choked up: 
	 - Uncle! Congratulations, it's an honor for you to win first prize in this difficult competition. I have something I want to tell you but I don't know if it's convenient. If you have young children, you will understand what I am about to say. My child has cancer and is in the hospital. If he doesn't have money for surgery, he probably won't survive! But my family… can't afford such a large amount of money… 
	 - So how much do you need? - The student looked at her and asked, truly sympathetic. 
	 After listening to the woman tell all the story, he immediately took the envelope containing the money he had just received and gave it to her. 
	 - Pray that your child can overcome the danger. Please go home and take care of her right away. - I said. 
	 - Thank you, I don't know how I can repay you. 
	After that, the woman with an emotional look turned and walked out the gate. A few days later he had the opportunity to return to school. One person saw it and immediately approached and asked: 
	- Someone told me that you met a woman the other night after the competition and you gave her money to treat her dying child, right? The young man nodded in confirmation. 
	 - Then I have to tell you this news so you know. She's a real scammer. She didn't have any children who were sick to the point of death. You are so gullible! You've been fooled, my friend! After a moment of silence, the young man asked again: 
	 - It's true that no child is sick to the point of death, right? 
	 - That's right. I guarantee it is. - The man asserted. 
	 - Oh, that's the best news I've heard all day. - The young man said. Then he added: 
	 - We should celebrate that no child has to die.
The good news

\t Dreams are neither available nor impossible. Dreams are paths that have not yet been shaped but that people will move towards and overcome.
On the first day of the school year, the chemistry professor of my class introduced himself to the students in the class and then spent time for us to get to know each other. As I stood up and looked around, I noticed a gentle hand placed on my shoulder. I turned around, there was a small old lady with wrinkled skin, looking at me with a smile that lit up her whole face.
She said:
\n\t - Hello, handsome guy. My name is Rose. I am 87 years old. Can I hug you?
I smiled and happily answered:
\n\t - Of course, ma\'am! - And she hugged me tightly.
\n\t - Why did she go to college at such an innocent and youthful age? - I asked jokingly.
She smiled:
\n\t - I came here to find a famous, soulful man to love and get together, have a few kids, and then retire and travel around the world.
\n\t - Are you serious? - I ask. I was curious to know what motivated her to want such a challenge at her age.
\n\t - I\'ve always dreamed of going to university and now I\'m living that dream! - She said.
After class ended, we went to the student union building and drank a glass of chocolate milk together. We became friends immediately. During the next three months, every day we left class together and talked about everything. I am always fascinated by this "time machine" when I hear her share her wisdom and life experiences with me.
\n\t Throughout the school year. Rose becomes an iconic figure at the university and easily makes friends with everyone. She liked to dress smartly, had character, and was happy with the attention other students focused on her. She always lived in that passion.
At the end of the school year, we invited Rose to speak at a reception and I will never forget what she taught us. She was introduced and walked up to the podium.
As she began her speech, she dropped a note on the floor. A little shy and confused, she picked up the microphone and said:
\n\t - Sorry ladies, I\'m a bit nervous. I\'ve given up beer and switched to Lent wine and it\'s killing me! I never plan what I\'m going to say, let me tell you simply what I really understand.
As we laughed, she regained her voice and began:
\n\t - We stop having fun because we get old; But actually we get old because we don\'t have fun anymore. There are only five secrets to staying young, happy and successful:
\n\t First, laugh and find humor in everyday life.
\n\t Second, see every day as a new day with new things. Anyone who lives by the past and prejudices of yesterday will not have the opportunity to believe and understand people. Please share your feelings with people who can share. Be persistent, believe in the human soul and don\'t look at one mistake to destroy all the good things that have come before and the good things that will come in the future. Don\'t be afraid to take risks to change your life.
\n\t Third, you must have a dream, an aspiration. When you lose those dreams, you will die. Too many of us have died that way and they don\'t even know it!
\n\t Fourth, there is a big difference between becoming older and becoming an adult. If you are 19 years old and lie in bed for a year without doing anything productive, you will become 20 years old. If I was 87 years old and stayed in bed for a year and didn\'t do anything, I would still become an 88-year-old woman. Any person must grow up and grow old. But that doesn\'t take away from your talents and abilities. The point is to grow by always finding opportunities to change.
\n\t Fifth, never regret. Adults often do not regret what they have done, but will regret what they did not do. Only people who are afraid of death have regrets.
She ended her talk by boldly singing the song “Rose Petals”. She sang that song with us and the lyrics have now become familiar to our daily lives.
And then. Rose also completed the college program she began many years ago. One week after graduation. Rose passed away peacefully in her sleep. More than two thousand students of the school attended her funeral with all respect and love for the wonderful woman who used her life as an example to prove that it is never too late to do everything. everything you can do in life.\n\n\n
Never give up on your dreams

\n\t My brother-in-law pulled out the bottom drawer of the desk where my sister often sat and worked and took out a package wrapped in tissue paper. He tore off the outer layer of paper and showed me a small pair of pants wrapped inside. The pants are very cute: made of soft silk with lace trim. There was still a price tag on it, not a small amount of money.
- Jan bought it when we first came to New York, 8 or 9 years ago, but she never wore it. She plans to save it for a special occasion. Now, besides this occasion, there is no other occasion.
He took the pants from me and placed them on the bed with the other clothes we planned to bury with my sister. He fiddled with it for a while then slammed the drawer shut and turned to me and said:
- Never hold anything back for a special occasion. Every day in this world is a special occasion.
His words kept echoing with me from that moment until the following days, when I helped him and my nephew arrange my sister\'s funeral. My sister passed away unexpectedly!
On the flight back home after her funeral, I kept thinking about those words, about all of my sister\'s unfulfilled dreams, about the things she did without realizing that they were special.
And I realized: life contains so many sweet flavors for us to enjoy whenever possible, not for us to cope with. So I decided to change!
I started reading more and worrying less about the little things. I enjoy looking at the scenery while sitting on the deck and don\'t get upset when I see weeds in the garden. I spend more time with family and friends and limit my participation in meetings that are not very useful.
I don\'t save anything anymore: I use all my beautiful china and crystal for every meaningful occasion - like losing a pound, the sink becoming clogged or cotton. The first camellia blooms.
I wear a nice shirt to the market if I feel like it. When I think I look classy, I can pay more for a small bag of vegetables without frowning. I will no longer save my most fragrant perfume for special occasions, no matter what the sales ladies or some other person whispers about.
I\'m gradually removing the phrases "someday" or "within a few days" from my vocabulary. If there\'s something worth seeing, hearing, or doing, I\'ll do it.
I\'m not sure what my sister would do if she knew that the next day she would no longer be in this world, the next day that we all take for granted will come. I think she must have called family members and a few close friends. Perhaps she made an appointment to meet some old friends to apologize and erase the unpleasant past events. Or she went out for a Chinese meal which I guess I will never know about!
The little things I don\'t get done will make me frustrated if I know my time is limited. Frustrated because I\'ve been putting off visiting good friends I plan to contact someday. Frustrated because I haven\'t written certain letters that I intended to write - within a few days.
I would be upset and regretful that I didn\'t regularly tell my husband and daughter how much I loved them. I\'m trying very hard not to delay, hold back or save anything that adds laughter and enriches our lives.
And every morning, when I wake up, I always tell myself: today is a special day. Every day, every minute, every breath… is a gift of life.
\n\t We don\'t know what might happen to us in life\'s strange and unexpected medley. However, we can decide what happens inside us, how we view it, how we perceive it, and what we do with it - and that\'s the key\n\n\n
Every day is a gift

\t You can have a bright start any time you want, because the so-called failure does not mean falling down but stopping in one place.
\n\t - Mary Picford
\n\t It was 1903. Mrs. Annie Johnson lived in Arkansas with her two sons and was in a dead end situation. Her money was almost exhausted, and she herself had no special abilities other than reading and adding simple numbers. Add to that her unsatisfying marriage and her segregated black background. Everything seemed to be pushing Annie into a dead end.
When she told her husband, William Johnson, that she was not satisfied with their marriage, he admitted that it was not what he expected and that he had long intended to study religion. He also said God called him to go on a mission trip to the Enid area of Oklahoma. However, he did not tell her that he knew a pastor there, with whom he would study and had a lovely, unmarried daughter. So they parted gently. Annie kept the house with only one room and Mr. William took most of the cash with him to Oklahoma.
Annie is a tall and energetic woman. She decided to start over and send her beloved children to someone else to look after. She said:
\n\t - I looked back at the road I was on and the distance that had passed. Because I was not satisfied, I decided to step off that road and turn to a new direction.
Knowing that she was unlikely to be hired to work at a cotton factory or a lumber mill in the area, she thought of a way to create a livelihood for herself based on these two factories.
She planned it meticulously and didn\'t let anyone know. One day, at dusk, to see if she was really ready to carry out her plan, she put the stones in two 19-liter buckets and carried them nearly five kilometers to the cotton factory. After resting for a while, she removed a few rocks and continued another 8 kilometers in the dark on a dusty road to the sawmill. On the way back to her small home with her children, she gradually removed the remaining stones along the way.
That night, she boiled chicken and fried ham. Then she kneaded the dough and made meat rolls. It was almost dawn before she went to sleep.
The next morning, she left home carrying burgers, fat, an iron pan and coal to make a fire. It was almost lunchtime when she appeared in an empty lot behind the cotton factory. When the lunch bell rang, she dropped the basil into the pan of boiling fat. The scent spread to the workers who had just come out of the factory, covered in white cotton dust and looking like ghosts.
\n\t Most of the workers had brought their own lunches, but today they were captivated by the aroma of the hot meat pies that Annie had just taken out of the pan. She wrapped them in greaseproof newspaper and sold them for 5 cents each. Even though sales were slow, in those first days Annie was very determined. She shares equally in sales at both factories.
So, if on Monday she sold hot, crispy cakes at the cotton mill and cold leftover cakes at the sawmill for three cents, then on Tuesday she would go to the sawmill first to greet the new cakes. when sawdust-covered sawyers appeared at the factory gate.
In the years that followed, on gentle spring days, hot summer afternoons, or cold, rainy and snowy days, Annie never disappointed her customers, who were sure to encounter the image of a The tall, dark-skinned woman bent over the oil pan, carefully turning each piece of burger. When she felt certain that the workers were loyal customers, she set up a booth between the two factories for them to come and eat.
In fact, she stepped off the path that seemed to have been chosen for her and found a completely new path for herself. Years later, that stall became a store where customers could buy anything from cheese, food, syrup, biscuits, candy, pickles, canned goods, fresh fruit, soft drinks , to coal, oil and even leather soles for worn shoes.
\n\t Each of us has the right and responsibility to consider the roads ahead, as well as the roads we have traveled. If the future path is not bright or does not promise us anything and we cannot turn back, we need to be determined, and only carry the necessary luggage, step off that path and turn to another direction. If the new choice is also unacceptable, don\'t be confused, let\'s be ready to change it.\n\n\n
New roads

When I was little, the clothes my dad wore always made me feel embarrassed. I want my dad to dress like doctors and lawyers, not the way I see him on hot mornings when he wakes up early to fry eggs for me and mom.

	 Dad likes to wear old jeans, with penknife marks on the crotch, and a cloth shirt with lots of keychains, holding all kinds of pens, cigarettes, glasses, wrenches, screwdrivers… screwdrivers in the pockets. Dad's shoes have steel toes and are very difficult to take off, so I sometimes take them off for him when he comes home from repairing the air conditioner. My father's profession also makes me feel terribly embarrassed. However, because I was still a child, I often sneaked into my father's room, imitated him wearing his clothes, and looked in front of the mirror. My imagination turned the tunic into a king's cape, and the belt into a soldier's holster. I often wear my father's bra to bed. It was thanks to the familiar smell of sweat on my father's collar that I overcame my fear of the dark. But in recent years, I've begun to wish my dad would sell his jeans in exchange for khaki pants and replace his old-fashioned shoes with more trendy flat-soled shoes. I also stopped wearing underwear to bed. And finally dreaming of another father.
I blame my father's way of dressing for the failures in my life. When boys bully me, I pray they see my dad wearing a cowboy hat, naked, and walking the dog. I felt like the girls were laughing at me because they saw my father wearing black shoes and mowing the lawn himself. Their family hired someone else to trim the lawn (I'm sure they dressed better than my father); while their father leisurely cruised the bay, wearing lemon yellow sweaters and expensive sandals. Dad only bought two suits in his life. Dad likes to dress comfortably so he can easily get under the car. However, on the day before my parents' 20th wedding anniversary, my dad and I went to Sears - a famous clothing store in the area. During the afternoon, Dad tried one set after another. For each set, Dad walked up to the mirror, smiled and nodded, asked the price and then went looking for another set. Dad probably tried on a dozen sets before driving by a discount store and buying one without even having to try it on. That night, my mother kept whispering that she had never seen a more handsome man.
However, the day my dad wore that outfit to attend my 8th grade award ceremony, I wished he would stay home. After the ceremony (I was selected as an Outstanding Student), my father changed my faded clothes and praised my achievements. When my father went into the garage to wash the car, I boldly told him everything about the alleged wrong that had humiliated me at the age of 14.

	 – Why doesn't dad dress "nicely" like your friends' dads? – I questioned.
Dad looked at me in shock with sad eyes, trying to find an answer. Then, before disappearing into the garage, Dad said: 
	 – Dad likes his outfit.
When I became more mature, I realized that the girls avoided me not because of my father, but because of me, his son. I realized that what Dad said that night clearly meant: “There are things more important than outer clothes; And I can't waste a single penny on myself because you need many things." Dad didn't need to say another word, but I understood what he wanted to say: "I sacrificed so that your life in the future will be better than mine."
At my high school graduation, my father attended in the new outfit my mother bought early in the morning. I don't understand why my dad seems taller, more handsome and more imposing than other dads. When Dad passed by, they gave way to him - of course not because of his clothes but because of who he was. Noticing the confidence in his father's dignified appearance and the pride in his eyes, the doctors and lawyers treated him politely and respectfully. Then when I got home, Dad put the most ordinary clothes from Sears in the closet. And until my father's funeral, I never saw it again! I don't know what my dad was wearing when he died. But Dad was working at that time so he must have been wearing his favorite outfit. That comforts me a lot. Mom planned to bury Dad in an outfit from Sears, but I convinced her to bring Dad's old jeans, cotton shirt, and worn-out shoes to the funeral home.
The morning of the funeral, I took a penknife and punched a hole in my father's belt so it fit my waist. After that, I put on my dad's Sears outfit. Gathering all my courage, I looked at myself in the mirror. There! Except for my clothes, I look so small and ordinary. Once again, like in my childhood, my clothes were loose and covered my skinny body. Dad's scent drifted across my face again, but it couldn't comfort me. I'm not sure about my father's physique – I stopped being a brash boy a long time ago. Standing silently in front of the mirror, tears welling up in my eyes, I tried to imagine "what I will be like in my next life" - the days when I will grow up in my father's clothes.
Dad\'s suit

Cherish love because love will last even when your golden health is gone.

	 A young man suffered from a serious illness and all treatments were ineffective against his condition. He was miserable thinking that he could die at any time, so he cut ties with everyone and locked himself in the house all day. But in the end, bored with the cramped situation and perhaps wanting to escape his own sadness and gloom, he decided to go out to the street once.
When passing by a music record store, the young man suddenly looked in. The ice shop is not large but is airy and the presentation is quite simple and pleasant. The salesperson was a girl probably just about his age. For a moment, he felt like the whole world had completely disappeared, leaving only him and the girl alone. He walked in front of her without looking at anything else.
The girl looked up at him, smiled and asked:

	 – What music do you need to buy?

	 And at that moment, he knew that his intuition was not wrong: it was the most beautiful smile he had ever seen in the world. He awkwardly replied:

	 – I… I want to buy a record.

	 Then he chose a plate and paid the girl.

	 – Do you want to package this record? – The girl asked, still with that innocent smile.

	From that day on, every day, he stopped by the store and bought a music record. Every time the girl wrapped it up for him carefully. He brought the disc home and put it in the closet without once taking it out to listen to it. He came to buy music just because he wanted to meet the sales girl. Although he really wanted to invite her out, he was too shy so he couldn't speak up. His mother seemed to know her son's feelings so she advised him to try to be bold once.
The next day, gathering all his courage, he placed a piece of paper with his phone number on the counter and quickly walked out…
Days passed, and one day, his phone rang and his mother picked up the phone. On the other end of the line, a young girl's clear voice rang out. That was the girl at the record store the other day. Suddenly the girl heard her mother's choking sound mixed with sobs: 
	 – Don't you know anything? My son passed away last week… 
	That evening, the mother walked into her son's room because she missed him so much. She opened her child's wardrobe and saw before her eyes stacks and stacks of music records still in their original wrappings. She picked up one and removed the wrapping paper. A small piece of paper fell, on it was a soft girl's handwriting: "Hello, I think you are so cute! Do you like to walk with me? Yen, Jacelyn.”
The mother took another record…
This time too, inside was a note: "Hello, I think you are very nice! Let's go for a walk together tonight! Yen, Jacelyn.”
Love is… after many struggles, we can overcome our shy, timid self to hold the hand of our beloved and say: "I Love You".
Late message

\n\n\n \t To keep the lamp burning, we must keep the lamp\'s oil tank full at all times.
\n\t -Mother Teresa \n\n\t During a luncheon, my friend Bonnie confided in me:
\n\t – Dave never said he loved me. Sometimes I think even he doesn\'t care about me anymore.
Knowing this couple well, I told her:
\n\t – Bonnie, he really loves you. Very clear.
\n\t – Do you think so? After twenty-seven years of marriage, things are no longer the same as the first few years.
I thought for a moment and then asked:
\n\t – I know how you feel, but why don\'t you try this? When you get home, look for his signs of love instead of looking for evidence to the contrary. Try it for twenty-four hours. Agree?
Bonnie agreed immediately.
The next day, Bonnie called me, her voice almost screaming:
\n\t – Your idea is effective! When I got home, Dave asked me if my lunch was good. I thought to myself, he wants to know it because he loves me. When he called me to watch the sunset, I thought, he said that means he loves me. In the middle of the night I woke up and couldn\'t get back to sleep, he asked if anything was wrong, and he punched me in the back… Many funny things started happening. First, I found him to be a great person. How else do I feel about the person who loves me? And then, just a moment later, when he was cranky, I thought, it\'s okay for him to be mad because I know he loves me.
I replied:
\n\t – That\'s good for you.
She giggled and continued:
\n\t – Drill. Not all. I started to feel different about myself. I\'m not as bad as before. Actually, I\'m much cuter.
Bonnie has learned her ability to change how she feels. Bonnie could return home to her husband unchanged, with the same prying attitude, and everything would be exactly the same. If Bonnie insists that her husband no longer loves her, she will lose the love that is still in its place.
Once, Bonnie often asked “Does he love me, or does he not love me?” But now Bonnie was surprised to discover the creative ways her husband found to answer the question burning in her heart: “Yes. He does love me.”\n\n\n
Love or not love?

\n\n\n \t Opportunity often comes under the guise of misfortune or in the guise of a temporary failure
\n\t – Napoleon Hill \n\n\t Tired after many days wandering around looking for work, the unemployed man felt extremely depressed and destitute. Then, one afternoon, luck smiled on him when he passed an interview to hire an employee for a large cleaning company. At the end of the conversation, the HR director told him:
\n\t – You will be hired for $5.35 an hour. Give me your e-mail address so we can work together easily. Our system will automatically send you all notifications for the day and show you where to file your first report.
Confused, the man said he was so poor he didn\'t have a computer and didn\'t even have an e-mail address.
At first, the director was surprised, but then he said coldly:
\n\t – You must understand that for a high-tech company like us, it is not acceptable for an employee to have an e-mail address. Sorry… Hi there. Stunned, the man turned and walked away. Only 10 bucks left in my pocket and I don\'t know where to go. He wandered to a market and saw a stall selling tomatoes with ripe red fruits. After buying all those tomatoes, he brought them to a crowded place in the downtown area and sold them. In less than 2 hours, he sold all his tomatoes and made double his investment. Excited by the results, he repeated the process several times until he could no longer walk. That day, he earned $100 and returned home with a bag of delicious food for his family.
From that day on, he started a tomato business.
Every day, he got up before dawn to pick up goods and sell them in a crowded downtown area. He worked so hard that it lasted all night. Soon the profits were multiplying rapidly.
In the second week, he bought a trailer that made transporting tomatoes less difficult. Then a month later, he sold the trailer to buy a pickup truck. By the end of the year, he owned three old trucks. His two eldest sons helped him with the business, his wife helped buy tomatoes, and his daughter decided to take a night accounting class at a community college to check the books for him. By the end of his sophomore year, he had a fleet of nice new trucks and recruited five more workers from the unemployed – all selling tomatoes. Although he was able to enjoy a comfortable life, he continued to work hard.
Time gradually passed. At the end of the fifth year, he owned a large company specializing in the production and sale of tomatoes. His company has created jobs for hundreds of unemployed and homeless people. The company\'s profits – as his daughter reports – surpassed one million dollars.
To ensure long-term development in the future, he decided to buy life insurance.
Taking the advice of his advisor, he signed an insurance policy that was suitable for his circumstances. In accordance with the procedure, the employee asked him for an e-mail address to send the necessary documents quickly. And when he answered that he did not have time to fumble with his computer, nor did he have an e-mail address, the consultant was surprised:
\n\t – What, you don\'t have an e-mail address? You don\'t even know the Internet? If he had all of these five years ago, I think his business would have been much more prosperous than it is now!
\n\t – No! – He smiled. – If I had e-mail 5 years ago, I would have been a worker all my life cleaning for $5.35 an hour!\n\n\n
Disadvantage or advantage?

\n\n\n\t Many people don\'t know what happiness is, not because they\'ve never had it, but because they\'ve never stopped to enjoy it.
\n\t – William Feather
\n\t Thirty days later, we are still following the trail – me and the whole Eskimo family. The weather was harsh, the cold and the wind seemed to freeze us, the temperature was down to minus 50 degrees, but the spirit of the Eskimo family was still strong. It can be said that this is the toughest journey I have ever experienced.
It seems that fate is trying to make it difficult for us. One day, a blizzard forced us to stay in tents. One day, due to a bad hunch of a local friend, we were forced to stop to build a new tent instead of moving on even though the weather was not very harsh. Many times I asked the Eskimo man, “How many days will it take us to reach the land of King William, but he never gave a straight answer. Eskimos don\'t like questions. They consider it rude. Only white people ask questions. Plus, Eskimos don\'t like to give answers. If you ask them, "What\'s the weather like tomorrow?", they\'ll just politely answer: "Mauna" (I don\'t know) even though they\'re super predictable, then act like they\'re busy. to the dogs to imply: “Why should I answer you? If I say it right, it won\'t solve anything, and if I answer it wrong, suddenly I\'ve made a fool of myself."
All morning and all afternoon we walked the frozen oceans and stopped only to examine the tracks the dogs had discovered or to leave the torches. We observe the land. Maybe We\'ll find out where we\'re looking. Then when a little hope had just flashed, the wind rose again, the snow covered thickly, erasing all traces, leaving us lost in despair in the midst of the vast white space.
We stopped again. Slowly, without haste in the native style, the Eskimos still accept life and fate. Ohudlerk – elderly man saying something to his wife and young daughter. If it were in France, during a storm, the farmer would pause equally calmly to examine the situation of the fields.
Unable to contain my uneasiness, I asked the man the familiar question again: "When do you think we\'ll get to King William\'s land?" And I don\'t know if repeating the same questions made him lose his temper or if that was what he was really concerned about. Only to see him turn to his wife and in their usual silence, they seemed to have just exchanged secret sympathy.
Then he came over and looked at me blankly. He said loudly – his voice was mixed with apprehension and trying to remain cautious:
\n\t – Aren\'t the dogs as good as you want them to be?
And then there was silence. The dogs turned their heads as usual as they prepared to continue their journey, and they were looking at me. The woman and the child pretended to be busy, but I knew they were also watching me surreptitiously. For a brief moment, everything seemed to stand still. That\'s the feeling Eskimos often plant in you when they leave you alone in tense silences. They made the silence even heavier. And will they stop like that? No, they let them go further. Finally, the man spoke, as if he could not contain his heart:
\n\t – Isn\'t that sled very good? Weren\'t you happy to see the snow covered the ocean during our journey?
He looked at me with reproachful eyes. I feel like an entire age of stone with its mysterious simplicity, Eastern wisdom, is looking at me, trying to understand - or perhaps more so, trying to understand myself. Then suddenly I felt like I could read the messages those old eyes were trying to say.
They say, “What\'s the hurry? And why do you always want to go on? What makes you keep worrying about the future when the present is so wonderful?".
That day, the man Eskimo taught me a lesson that I will never forget. Because I was so busy thinking about the future, I forgot the importance of the present. His words reminded me that someone once told me: "Thinking about the past is to regret, thinking about the future is to be afraid. But what about the present? Isn\'t the present the easiest to understand?
The world is nothing but a reflection of reality through the human mind. For me, the North Pole is an inspiration, a desire to explore, but for the Eskimo family, it is a huge kingdom that they are the owners. For me, frost and frost are hardships and challenges, but for them, it is a blessing, a gift from the creator. From thousands of glasses looking at life, we are free to choose between suffering and hope.
We are busy crossing the highways of life and indifference to the landscapes on either side. Someone once said: “The great life consists of moments of leisure” – moments of rest, and reflection. The Eskimos stop when they are satisfied even though tomorrow awaits them. And for them, tomorrow may be the lurking of outside forces who are eager to sow the garbage of hunger and death. So when the god of death has not yet come, they happily enjoy, boldly live and discover the beautiful life, leaving all regrets behind.
When I read the messages that Ohudlerk gave me through my eyes, it was also when I realized how poor my soul was before those brief moments in the midst of the great Arctic ice and snow. From there, I learned a valuable lesson that we must cherish and cherish each day, that nothing in the future can change what we are holding in the present.
In Vancouver, after finishing my arduous journey, I rushed into the hotel as if I didn\'t want to lose another minute, and then suddenly, I stopped in the middle of the crowd. The siren to get out of the way sounded from all directions, but I didn\'t hear it. I felt like Ohudlerk was standing on the road ahead, watching me with his deep eyes, full of wisdom and worry and wonder, and then he asked me if the dogs were dogs good and is the white snow not really God\'s gift.
I suddenly laughed. We are so silly! I thought to myself. And now, I still think so.
\n\t – Gontran de Poncins. \n\n\n
Lessons from the Eskimos

	 The worker I hired to renovate the farm had just finished his first hard day of work. When the door opened, he changed his attitude surprisingly. His face relaxed with a bright smile - his first smile of the day. 	 – Oh, that's the tree that relieves my troubles. – He explained. – I know I cannot avoid worries and troubles at work, but one thing I am sure is that those troubles do not belong to my small house. \n\n\n\t My friend is the owner of a horse farm in San Ysidro, his name is Monty Roberts. His horse farm is a place where fundraisers regularly take place to help young people in the area carry out their projects. Once, we heard him tell a story like this:
\n\t “A long time ago, there was a poor boy who followed his father day after day from stable to stable, from racetrack to racetrack, from farm to farm to help father trains horses.
One day, his teacher asked the students to write about their dreams. While other students wanted to become engineers, doctors, football players, actors… the boy wrote about his dream, that one day he would be the owner of a farm. horse. He even drew a diagram of the stable, clearly showing the locations of all the buildings, stables, and racetrack.
For that day\'s writing, the boy only received a big F with a note from the teacher: "See you again after class." And here are the words the boy heard from his teacher:
“This is a pipe dream for a child like me. I\'m not capable of doing that. Do you know how much money is needed to own a horse farm? What is the money to buy stallions, buy land to build a farm… You should define your goals more realistically. If you rewrite another essay, I will reconsider your score."
During that week, the boy thought a lot. He decided to ask his father what he should do. His father said:
\n\t – Hey son, you have to decide for yourself. And I think this is very important for you.
Finally, after days of pondering, he decided to return his old work to the teacher without making any changes. He boldly said:
\n\t – Teacher, I would like to keep my dream and agree to accept that bad grade."
At the end of the story, Monty Roberts said:
\n\t – I tell you this story because you are sitting in the middle of my 200-acre horse farm. I still have that test, framed above the fireplace. – Pause for a moment, he added. – An interesting thing is that in the summer two years ago, my old teacher took his students to camp here for a whole week. Before saying goodbye, he said to me: "Monty, you taught me the lesson about willpower to live your dream." \n\n\n
Live your dream

One beautiful morning, a group of frogs invited each other into the forest for a walk. Due to carelessness, two frogs accidentally slipped and fell into a deep hole. In a dangerous situation, the frogs in the group rushed to the edge of the hole to find a way to rescue. However, after trying everything, they found the hole was too deep to save the two unfortunate frogs. The group desperately told the two frogs in the hole this harsh truth and told them that they could only wait for death.
Ignoring those comments, the two frogs tried their best to jump out of the hole. But instead of encouraging them, the other frogs advised them not to waste their energy but to accept their fate as soon as possible. After unsuccessful efforts, one frog followed the advice of the frogs on the shore, gave up and fell to his death in despair.
Meanwhile, the remaining frog continues to jump. Even though the group of frogs kept repeating the previous advice, he still did not give up his efforts and jumped harder and harder. Finally he was able to jump ashore. At this time, a group of frogs surrounded him and asked: "Didn't you hear what we said?". It turns out this frog has hard of hearing. He thought the frogs had been encouraging him all this time.
Every word we say contains immense power. A word of encouragement can become a driving force to help people who are in a deadlock regain their spirit and overcome difficulties. But there are also words that can kill a person in a state of despair. Therefore, be careful with what you say. Don't destroy the spirit of a person in a difficult situation with negative words. Instead, take the time to motivate and encourage them. How our lives and those around us turn out depends on our own attitudes and words.
The power of words

\n\n\n\t My parents-in-law had just returned from New York from a horrible winter break in Florida. Over the phone, my mother told me that when my parents arrived in North Carolina, the car broke down. They took it to repair but then it broke again in Delaware. “But, the worst thing is probably still the minute shoes covered in smoke because of congestion on Verrazano Bridge. At that time, we felt like he would never come home again. "- said the mother.
\n\t “It\'s horrible. ” – I said, and really wanted to share my story – the tragedy when my car stalled at 9:30 p.m. in an empty parking lot in the mall.
But at that moment someone knocked on the door, so we had to drop the conversation. Before hanging up, Mom added that: \n\t "Thanks for listening, but I\'m most grateful that you didn\'t tell the story about that terrible broken car."
My face was hot with embarrassment. Why can mom read my mind so clearly? Days later, I still have doubts about this.
I can\'t count how many times I complained about my disagreements with my son, my frustrations with work, problems with my car… that my friend had to interrupt and complain. "Those things happen to me too."
And then, from time to time, we were engrossed in talking about her rebellious son, her fussy boss, and her leaky fuel tank. I couldn\'t do anything but nod at the right time, but in my heart I couldn\'t help but wonder if we were all indifferent to other people\'s feelings or not.
It is easy to confuse “I understand how you feel because I have been through it too” with genuine sympathy. There\'s nothing more natural than trying to soothe a grieving friend than making sure she\'s not alone.
These sorrows are similar only in a certain way, but in detail, they are as colorful as fingerprints. The statement: “I understand your pain” is just the prelude to a series of pieces of advice that follows: Here\'s what I\'ve done, and here\'s what you should do, etc. v. But when your car trip lasts three times the usual time or when your child has a high fever in the middle of the night, do you really want to hear how your friend handled a similar situation? ?
When we feel sad, confused or happy, what we want most is the sharing of a friend who is ready to listen to us at any time. Listening to be in tune with the pain or joy of another is the manifestation of true empathy.
Thankfully, empathy is a virtue we can easily learn. Since that conversation with my mother-in-law, I have stopped the habit of talking to others while they are confiding. I\'ve learned to listen to and respect their emotional circuits, paying more attention to their body language, facial expressions, tone of voice, and unspoken implications.

	 – I know you are always kind and full of love. I beg You to turn me into a Rose! The fairy looked intently at the flower: 
	 – Do you know what you are asking for? One day you will regret it.
But Violet still insisted. Moved by her desire, the fairy finally agreed. She touched Violet's body with her magical finger, and immediately Violet turned into a beautiful rose tree, proudly rising high with bright red flowers on its branches. One day, Thunderstorm passed through the garden, breaking tree branches, uprooting even tall trees. The whole garden was battered in the wind and storm, except for the small flowers that lay close to the ground like Violet. The storm cleared. Clear blue sky again. Violet girls waved purple flower branches and played together. A girl looked at the Rose - Violet back in the day - pityingly: 
	 – Look, she is paying the price for her temporary desire! Miss Rose lay on the ground, her body broken, her flowers and leaves tattered, trying to use her last breath to whisper: 
	 -I have never been afraid of Thunderstorms. When I was a little Violet, there were times when I felt comfortable and satisfied with myself. But when I kept doing that, I suddenly felt small, boring and bland. I don't want to live a life where I only cling to the ground all year round with fear and weakness, and when winter comes, I will be buried under a layer of white snow. Today, although I am about to say goodbye to you, I am very happy and satisfied because I have learned what the colorful world above is like. Salt

One time, when the young man complained about studying but not making progress, the teacher listened quietly, then gave him a full spoonful of salt and a small glass of water.

	 -Put this spoon of salt in a glass of water, then drink it!
The young man immediately followed suit and tried drinking the salty, bitter drink. The teacher took him to a nearby lake and poured a spoon full of salt into the water.

	 -Now taste the water in the lake!

	 -The water in the lake is still the same, teacher. It's not salty at all 
	 -The boy said as he scooped up some water from the lake and tasted it.
The teacher slowly said:

	 -My child, everyone has difficulties at times, it's just like this spoon of salt. But each person dissolves it in a different way. People with open hearts are like a lake, sadness does not make them lose their joy and love of life. But for those whose souls are only as small as a glass of water, they will make their lives bitter and never learn anything useful for themselves!

	 That's right, if I hold it for a minute there's nothing worth mentioning. But if I hold it for an hour, my hands get tired. If you hold it for a day, you will call an ambulance for me. Same weight, but the longer you carry it, the heavier it becomes.

In a quiet room. It was so silent that we could hear the candles talking. There are four candles burning and they confide in each other.

	 The first candle said: “I am the fire symbolizing Harmony. But at this moment, we are very unfortunate. People always cause war and hatred for each other, so should we still exist or not? “. Having finished speaking, the candle slowly dimmed and then completely extinguished.

	 The second candle continued: “And I, am a symbol of Love. But ironically, today people have almost completely forgotten us. Everyone is jealous and envious of each other. Even brothers in the same family are the same. I'm so bored." Having finished speaking, the candle also went out.

	 Next, the third candle spoke: “I am Faith. But in life now, no one needs us anymore. I become a person of excess and luxury. Humans now only run after practical things and never believe in themselves. Here I go.”. After speaking, it slowly turned off and emitted a white smoke.

	 The room then became dark and cold. There is only one last candle burning, like a lonely star at the end of the horizon. Suddenly, a boy walked in and said: “Why don't you guys burn anymore? This world still needs you.”

	 At that time, the fourth candle spoke: “Don't worry. I am Hope. If I am still burning, even if the flame is fragile, we can still light up Harmony - Love and Faith." The boy's eyes lit up. And he used the fourth candle - the Hope candle to relight the other extinguished candles.
are you poor?

\n\n\n\t One day, a rich father took his son to the countryside to show him how the poor people lived. They found a farm belonging to the second poorest family in the area.
“This is a way to teach children to appreciate those whose lives are more miserable than theirs.” – the father thought it was a practical lesson for his little child.
After staying and learning about life here, they returned home. On the way home, the father looked at his son and smiled: "How was the trip?"
– That\'s great, dad! -You have seen how poor people live! -Oh, yes. -So what did you learn from this trip?
The child did not hesitate: -You see we have one dog, they have four. Our house has a swimming pool that goes to the middle of the yard, and they have an endless river. We have to put the lights in the garden, they have twinkling stars at night. If our porch only reaches the front yard, they have the whole horizon. We have a piece of land to live on and they have long fields. We must have people to serve, and they must serve others. We have to buy food, and they grow it. We have protective walls around us, and they have neighbors who protect each other…
At this point the father said nothing. “Dad, I already know how poor we are..”- the boy added.
\n\t Many times we forget what we have and only always ask for what we don\'t have.
There are also things that have no value to one person but are desirable to another. That depends on each person\'s perspective and assessment. Please don\'t worry too much, wait for what you don\'t have yet and forget what you do have, even though they are very small.

\n\n\n\t Two children wrapped in oversized, tattered overcoats stood next to each other behind the door, tremblingly inviting me: "Miss, do you buy used newspapers?"
I was busy and just wanted to say no, but when I looked down at their feet, I couldn\'t bear it. Tiny sandals, soaked from snow and rain. “Come inside, I\'ll make you each a cup of hot cocoa!” They quietly followed me. Two pairs of soggy sandals were placed on the mantelpiece to dry.
Cocoa and toast served with jam can warm your heart against the bitter cold outside. After giving the children food, I went back to the kitchen to continue with the painful spending numbers.
The quiet atmosphere in the living room made me feel a bit strange. I looked into the room.
The girl was holding the empty cup in her hand, looking at it passionately. The boy accompanying him timidly said: "Miss, are you rich?"
“Are you rich? No, no, dear!” – As I spoke, I looked sadly at my old, worn tablecloth.
The girl carefully placed the cup on the saucer. “Your cups match your plates so well!” The girl\'s voice sounded hungry.
Then they left, holding old newspaper packages in their hands, freezing in the bitterly cold wind. They don\'t say thank you. But really, they don\'t need to thank me. What they did for me is more than a thank you. My plain blue ceramic cups and saucers are plain. But they are a very good set. I tasted the potatoes and stirred the soup. Potatoes and soup, a roof over my head, my husband with a stable job – it all suits me very well.
I put the chair in front of the fireplace back in its original place and tidied up the room. The mud from the two children\'s wet sandals still lingered on the mantelpiece, but I didn\'t wipe it away. I want to keep them, in case one day I forget how rich I am.

My father

\n\n\n\t At that time, I was 16 years old. One morning, my father asked me to drive him to the remote village of Mijar, 18 miles from home, and told me to take the car for repair at a nearby garage. Because I had just learned to drive and felt this was a good opportunity to practice, I immediately agreed. I drove my father to the village and promised to pick him up at 4pm and then take the car to the garage. Since it would take several hours to wait, I decided to buy a ticket to the movie theater across the street. Being absorbed in the movie, I forgot the concept of time and when I was startled to glance at the clock, it was already 6 o\'clock…
I knew my father would be angry when he found out I had gone to the movies and would probably never let me drive again, so I immediately thought of some other problem with the car to explain why I was late.
I drove to the meeting place and saw my father waiting patiently on the corner. I apologized to him for being late and said that I had tried to come as soon as possible but the car needed some other repairs. I will never forget the way he looked at me at that time…
\n\t – I\'m very disappointed that you had to lie to me, Jason.
\n\t – What! That\'s the truth, Dad.
He looked back at me:
\n\t – When you didn\'t arrive on time, I called the garage to ask if there was a problem and they said you hadn\'t come to pick up the car yet.
A feeling of guilt filled my soul and I immediately confessed to my father the real reason I was late.
\n\t – Father is very angry, not with his child but with himself. Dad realized that he was not a good father. After so many years, I still feel like I have to lie to you. It\'s heartbreaking to raise a son who can\'t even tell the truth to his father. Now I will walk home and think about what I did wrong all these years.
\n\t – But dad, it\'s 18 miles from here to home. It\'s dark again, I can\'t walk.
All my protests and apologies are useless. I disappointed my father and I also learned the most painful lesson of my life. Father started walking along the dark road filled with dust and wind. I slowly drove behind him, begging all the way in the hope that he would forgive me, but my father still walked quietly and with austere contemplation.
\n\t The image of my father walking tiredly and in pain are memories that I will never forget. But it was also the most meaningful lesson because I have never lied to him since then.

He slowed down, but when the car passed by where he saw the child, there was no one there. Suddenly, he heard the sound of rocks being thrown at his car door. He immediately stepped on the brake and turned the car around back to where the stone was thrown. There was indeed a child standing among the parked cars. Jumping out of the car, not having time to look around, he grabbed the child, pressed him against a nearby car and shouted: "What the hell are you doing?". Anger rose to the top of his head, he continued: "This car is brand new, you will have to pay a lot of money for your stone."

	 “Please, sir. I'm sorry. I don't know what else to do" - the boy pleaded - "I threw the stone because I waved but no one stopped the car…". 	 Approaching the fallen child, the man tried to swallow something blocking his throat. He lifted the baby up and placed it in the wheelchair, then pulled out a towel and awkwardly tried to wipe off the stains and examined everything carefully.
